html:
The Kakataibo, also called Cashibo, are a Panoan people of the Amazon foothills of central Peru, on the Aguaytía and San Alejandro rivers between Huánuco and Ucayali.

Their language is related to that of the Shipibo-Konibo and other Panoan peoples. Some Kakataibo groups still avoid contact with outsiders in the forests of the Cordillera Azul, and in 2021 Peru set aside a reserve to protect them. Logging, coca growing and the road from Lima to Pucallpa have brought conflict to their land. See also the Iskonawa, another small Panoan people.
